notes: Summary: CompileWise builds an IDE-native copilot for enterprise developer teams (large monorepos, private registries).
Use-case focus: low-latency completions with relevant repo context (function-level and PR-level), aggressive chunking to fit long repositories.
Key ask: embeddings + vector DB must be kept inside customer VPC; any hosted index unacceptable for core codebase.
Latency target: <50ms per token for inline completions; end-to-end RTT budget ~80-120ms depending on model size.
Throughput: concurrent users ~500 active devs; peak bursts during CI runs for batch code search reranking.
Model strategy: want to pin L2 small models for completions, allow larger L1 models for heavy refactor flows. Need per-route/version pinning UI.
Streaming: IDE needs token-level streaming with deterministic ordering; client-side resume on reconnect required.
Embeddings: experimenting with repo-aware chunking (file-level + function-level) and hybrid retrieval (hnsw + ssd-backed store).
Vector DB: preference for self-hosted vector store (we suggested Milvus/Weaviate options), but license compatibility is a blocker.
Privacy: legal: 'No customer code can be used for model training' - must confirm retention controls and explicit non-training clause.
Quotes: Rina - 'We need completions that actually understand our monorepo context — cross-package references are critical.'
SE notes: observed KV-cache cold starts impacting first-completion latency, recommended prefix caching + eager KV warmup.
Cost sensitivity: high — engineering headcount limited; they care about per-token cost at 100M+ tokens/month scale.
POC scope doc link in drive; deliverables: latency/throughput matrix, cost projection, residency and KMS test plan.
product_requirements: Low-latency streaming (sub-50ms token in-editor) with resume support
Model/version pinning per route and per-team
Embeddings pipeline that supports chunking strategies: file, function, semantic slices
Vector DB deployment inside VPC with snapshot/backup integration to KMS
Prefix and KV-cache warmup to mitigate first-token jitter
Automatic fallback routing to smaller models under load with deterministic quality thresholds
